images.title: A number and its reverse
images.purpose: Shows the move every practice item uses: a two digit number ab is 10a + b, its reverse is 10b + a.
images.composition: Two digit tile pairs, one above the other, each with its place value form to the right.
images.exact_structure: Upper row: two square tiles side by side, a in teal #0072B2 then b in amber #E69F00, an arrow, then 10a + b. Above the upper tiles, small grey words: tens over the first tile, ones over the second. Lower row: two tiles b in amber then a in teal, an arrow, then 10b + a. In each expression a is teal and b is amber. Nothing else is drawn. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, which is large and centred; no scenery, no people, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Write each digit times its place, then simplify.
images.description: Shows the move every practice item uses: a two digit number ab is 10a + b, its reverse is 10b + a.
images.context: Practice picture for decoding divisibility tricks.
images.teaching_notes: Adding the two gives 11a + 11b; subtracting gives 9 times the digit difference.

image_decisions.why: Practice has no tool; the place value form is the one manipulation every item needs.
